paper_title: Search for ultralight axion dark matter in a side-band analysis of a 199Hg free-spin precession signal
suggested_experiment_name: PSI-HgM-sideband (199Hg free-spin precession, nEDM apparatus at PSI)
coupling_convention: g_aNN in GeV^-1 as plotted on the y-axis (axion-nucleon coupling divided by f_a-type normalization; NOT dimensionless g_an)
notes: Measured 95% C.L. exclusion on axion-nucleon coupling g_aNN from side-band analysis of 199Hg free-spin precession at PSI (2017 nEDM apparatus data), covering 1e-16 eV < m_a < 1e-13 eV with peak sensitivity g_aNN ~ 3.5e-6 GeV^-1. The 199Hg system is predominantly sensitive to the axion-NEUTRON coupling (factor ~10 weaker dependence on g_app), so AxionNeutron is assigned; the exclusion plot assumes g_ann = g_app. No numerical table available: data points are reconstructed from the text peak sensitivity plus the analytic scaling in Eq. (13) where the limit is proportional to the sideband frequency offset (i.e., roughly proportional to m_a), so intermediate values are approximate and do not capture insensitive regions at multiples of f_Hg = 7.879 Hz or the noise dip near 4 Hz. Conservative rho_DM = 0.4 GeV/cm^3 assumed. Paper also gives a factor-10-better projection for the n2EDM apparatus (dashed line), not extracted here. | selector: figure_vision over text (quality (1, 1, 1, 1, 2, 0, 0.65, 34)) | Vision: Exclusion plot (paper Fig. 4) shows g_aNN [GeV^-1] vs axion Compton frequency (bottom, 0.02-100 Hz) and axion mass (top, ~1e-16 to 4e-13 eV). Traced the lower boundary of the red 'PSI-HgM-sideband' region (95% CL). Mass converted via m[eV]=4.136e-15*f[Hz]. Boundary rises roughly linearly (log-log slope ~1) from ~3e-6 GeV^-1 at 0.024 Hz to ~8e-5 at 1 Hz, with a sensitivity-dip bump near 4-4.5 Hz (peak ~1.3e-3), then a wiggly plateau ~8e-4 to 1.2e-3 up to ~20 Hz. Paper states Hg is primarily sensitive to g_ann (factor ~10 weaker dependence on g_app), plot assumes g_ann = g_app; hence AxionNeutron. Insensitive notches at multiples of the 7.879 Hz carrier are not depicted in the plot.
